title: Choices for Increased Mobility Act of 2026
official_summary:
Choices for Increased Mobility Act of 2026

This act requires the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) to establish specific billing codes under Medicare for certain materials used in ultralightweight manual wheelchairs.

Specifically, the CMS must establish at least two billing codes for the base of the wheelchair, with at least one code for a base with titanium or carbon fiber construction material and at least one code for a base without these materials. Suppliers receive the same payment under Medicare for these wheelchairs as would otherwise apply, but may bill beneficiaries for any difference between the payment and the actual charge for the wheelchair. The CMS may require suppliers to inform beneficiaries of their potential financial liability in these cases.

summary.headline: New law makes Medicare create separate billing codes for ultralightweight manual wheelchairs built from titanium or carbon fiber.
summary.what_it_does: Medicare must set up at least two billing codes for the base of ultralightweight manual wheelchairs: one for bases made of titanium or carbon fiber and one for bases made of other materials. Medicare pays suppliers the same amount it would have paid anyway. Suppliers may charge the patient the difference between Medicare's payment and the wheelchair's actual price. Medicare may require suppliers to tell patients ahead of time that they could owe this extra cost.

who_it_affects.group: Medicare beneficiaries who use ultralightweight manual wheelchairs
who_it_affects.how: They may be able to get titanium or carbon fiber wheelchairs through Medicare but could be billed for the price difference above what Medicare pays.
They must use the new billing codes and may bill patients for costs above Medicare's payment, possibly with a duty to warn patients about those costs first.
The agency must create the new billing codes and may set rules on telling patients about their costs.
